title: Initial dynamic-programming value
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a finite bit string, and let $s,V$ be natural numbers. Suppose there is a function $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that on every input and every choice string, the total number of work-tape cells visited by $N$ is at most $sp$ of the input length; suppose $sp(|x|)\le s$ and $2^{K(s+\ell(|x|)+1)}\le V$, where $K$ is the configuration-code constant of $N$ and $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$. If there is a natural number $T$ such that every choice string of length $T$ makes $N$ halt on input $x$, then the depth-$V$ dynamic-programming value at the code of the initial configuration, viewed as a rational number, equals $2^V$ times the probability that $N$ outputs exactly $[1]$ on input $x$ under a uniformly random choice string of length $V$.
